stance.label: Taiwan breaks its 200-day line · still a pullback by the rules · stay on plan

headline: Taiwan crashes 6%, 2nd-biggest point drop ever; institutions sell NT$114B, index breaks 200-day
summary: Today was panic selling in Taiwan, not yet a confirmed trend turn: the TAIEX closed 0.8% below its 200-day line, and the rules need 5 closes below with a flat line to call it weak. All three institutional groups sold, and investment trusts ended a 24-day buying streak. Nvidia earnings early Wednesday Taipei time are the next test. Keep regular investing on plan.

watch.label: TAIEX 200-day line
watch.note: Closed 41,040.08 on 11/16, 0.8% below the line; weak only after 5 closes below and a flat line

watch.label: TAIEX bear line (−20% from high)
watch.note: About 3% away; a break means a bear market by definition

overview.lead: Taiwan saw broad panic selling today: the TAIEX fell 2,635 points to 41,040, its second-biggest point drop ever, and closed at the day's low.
points: TSMC (2330) fell 5.7% to NT$2,215, back below its 200-day line.
MediaTek (2454) fell 7.9%, erasing Friday's limit-up rally in one day.
Electronics heavyweights led the fall: Delta Electronics (2308) hit limit-down and Hon Hai (2317) fell 9.3%.
2,137 listed and OTC stocks fell and only 304 rose, so there was almost nowhere to hide.
The OTC index fell 6.8%, deeper than the TAIEX.
A market rumor says Nvidia (NVDA) Vera Rubin volume could slip to the first half of 2027. It is unconfirmed, but it crushed PCB and substrate stocks.

focus.lead: Among the nine tracked names, the pressure sits on the three Taiwan ones: 0050 fell 5.9% today, and the NAVs of Allianz Taiwan Technology, Cathay Taiwan High Dividend and Neuberger Berman Taiwan-Japan do not yet reflect the crash.
points: Yuanta Taiwan 50 (0050) closed at 96.45, back under 100, but still 0.8% above its 200-day line.
0050 held up better than the TAIEX: the index broke its 200-day line, 0050 did not.
Cathay Taiwan High Dividend (TW000T3786A8): its top two, TSMC and MediaTek, fell 5.7% and 7.9% today; the next NAV will show it.
Allianz Taiwan Technology (TW000T3604Y3): Unimicron and TSMC are among its top three and were in today's hardest-hit group; its 47% one-year volatility is the highest of the nine.
Neuberger Berman Taiwan-Japan (TW000T5011A9): its largest holding Jentech is a cooling stock, and peer Asia Vital Components (3017) fell 9.9% today.
NAV dates: Neuberger Berman Taiwan-Japan to 11/12, the other five funds to 11/13; SPY and QQQ are also at the 11/13 close.

position.lead: No new add tier was hit today; 0050 is still 15% from tier 5, so the framework needs no extra action.
points: 0050 has used four tiers; tier 5 at 81.55 is 15.4% away.
QQQ tier 3 at 645.71 is 5% away (11/13 close).
SPY tier 2 at 701.18 is 7.1% away (11/13 close).
AB International Technology (LU0060230025) tier 5 at 1,219 is 10.9% away (11/13 NAV).
Fidelity Japan Value (LU0997587083) tier 5 at 41.75 is 15% away (11/13 NAV).
Allianz Taiwan Technology and Cathay Taiwan High Dividend have used all tiers, so today's drop triggers nothing new.

macro.lead: No new US data today, and rates remain the second weight on tech: the 10-year yield sits high at 5.15%.
points: The 10-year Treasury yield is 5.15% (11/13), still high at the long end.
The high-yield spread is 3.2% (11/12), so credit shows no stress.
China's October retail sales and industrial output missed forecasts, adding doubt about Asian demand.
The Taiwan dollar is at 32.94 (11/13), down 0.75 in a month, not yet a sharp drop.

sentiment.lead: Taiwan sentiment is in a washout zone but not yet oversold: 3 bottoming signals are on, and RSI 37 is still above the oversold line.
points: 172 stocks hit new lows and only 6 hit new highs, so the new-lows light came on today.
Only 14% of stocks are above their 50-day line, and about one in five are above the 200-day line.
Yuanta Taiwan 50 Inverse (00632R) rose about 5% intraday as hedging demand poured in.
US VIX is 19.3 (11/13), so US sentiment has not joined the panic.

sectors.lead: There was no safe haven today, only smaller and bigger losses: electronic components fell 9.4%, and only IT services, home living and food edged up.
points: Electronic components fell 9.42% and lost a third of their value in a month.
Optoelectronics fell 8.4% and glass and ceramics fell 9.7%, as last week's leaders gave back gains together.
Copper-clad laminate, ABF substrate and high-end PCB stocks hit limit-down; the Vera Rubin delay rumor hit the top of the AI supply chain.
4 cybersecurity stocks hit limit-up against the tide, among the few pockets of buying.

taiwan.lead: Institutions pulled back across the board: the three groups sold NT$114B, and even steady investment trusts ended a 24-day buying streak.
points: Foreign investors sold NT$70.2B, flipping to selling one day after Friday's buying.
Investment trusts sold NT$18B, ending 24 straight days of buying since 10/8.
Dealers sold NT$25.9B, mostly in hedging accounts.
Foreign net short TAIEX futures stand at 96,787 contracts, down about 5,000 over five days, so futures did not add shorts.
Margin data only runs to 11/13, down 17.6% over 20 days; today's forced selling will show tomorrow.
Listed turnover was NT$845.1B, heavy-volume selling.

watch.lead: Watch three things next: whether the TAIEX regains its 200-day line within 5 days, US retail sales tomorrow night, and Nvidia earnings early Wednesday.
points: The TAIEX 200-day line is 41,382; today it closed 0.8% below.
A break of 39,858 is 20% off the high, a bear market by definition.
US October retail sales come out 11/17 21:30 Taipei time.
Nvidia reports 11/17 after the US close, 11/18 early morning Taipei, its first talk on orders and shipments since the CEO change.
Minutes of the October FOMC come out early 11/19 Taipei time.

regime.lead: By the rules, Taiwan is still in a pullback, not a turn to bear: the call is still "correction in an uptrend", it is only day 1 below the 200-day line, and only 1 risk light is on.
points: Trend: the TAIEX closed 0.8% below its 200-day line, which is still rising; it turns weak after 5 closes below and a flat line.
The S&P 500 is still 3% above its 200-day line (11/13), an ongoing uptrend.
Systemic risk lights: 0 globally; credit, the economy and financial conditions show no problem yet.
The closest to turning on is the high-yield spread at 3.2%, still far from 5%.
Taiwan has only 1 light on, breadth collapse, with about one in five stocks above the 200-day line.
Bottoming signals: 3 on in Taiwan, deleveraging, breadth washout and a surge in new lows; the extreme foreign selling light switched off.
History: from here Taiwan usually fell further; 10 of all 11 episodes went past −20%.
3 of the 4 fast episodes went past −20%; too few samples, for reference only.
What would flip the call: 5 closes below 41,382 with a flat line means weak.
A break of 39,858 (−20% from high) means a bear market by definition.
